Dr. Eda Şensu Demir

Research Statement

I am a food scientist specializing in the bioactive potential of marine macroalgae, with expertise in green extraction technologies, bioactive peptide characterization, and nano/micro-encapsulation. Through nationally and internationally funded projects, my research bridges marine biotechnology and food science to develop functional ingredients and nutraceuticals with demonstrated health-promoting properties.

Research Areas

Marine Bioactive Peptides

ACE-inhibitory and antioxidant peptides from macroalgae

Nano & Micro-Encapsulation

Protecting bioactives through gastrointestinal digestion

Green Extraction Technologies

Ultrasound-assisted enzymatic protein recovery

Metabolomics & Neuroprotection

Anti-Alzheimer potential of brown macroalgae

Functional Food Development

Translating marine bioactives into health-promoting ingredients

Current Projects

Anti-Alzheimer Potential of Brown Macroalgae (TÜBİTAK 2219)

Evaluation of the neuroprotective potential of bioactive compounds obtained from brown macroalgae via a sustainable biorefinery approach using metabolomics and cell-based models, in collaboration with GEOMAR Helmholtz Centre for Ocean Research Kiel.

Phlorotannin-Rich Extracts for Food Shelf Life (CORNET)

Utilization of phlorotannin-rich extracts from cultivated macroalgae to extend food shelf life and valorization of extraction wastes as animal feed, in partnership with Fraunhofer-Gesellschaft.

Research Impact

My work aims to bridge marine biotechnology and food science by translating laboratory-scale discoveries into scalable, sustainable solutions. Through the development of advanced encapsulation systems and green extraction methodologies, I strive to unlock the full health-promoting potential of marine-derived bioactives — from ACE-inhibitory peptides with antihypertensive relevance to phlorotannins with neuroprotective promise — ultimately contributing to the design of functional foods and nutraceuticals grounded in rigorous scientific evidence.
